ingredients.display: Extra-virgin olive oil (preferably Italian, if not Italian then Tunisian, French, and Greek are advisable)
ingredients.raw: Extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] (preferably Italian, if not Italian then Tunisian, French, and Greek are advisable)

ingredients.display: ½ head of garlic (or less), minced

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons dried [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red chile flakes]]

ingredients.display: 1 cup (240 g) fresh basil, finely torn or roughly chopped and reserved
ingredients.raw: 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) fresh [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], finely torn or roughly chopped and reserved

ingredients.display: 2 medium to large onions (preferably red or yellow), diced
ingredients.raw: 2 medium to large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]] (preferably red or yellow), [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]

ingredients.display: 1 yellow bell pepper, cut into strips
ingredients.raw: 1 yellow [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], cut into strips

ingredients.display: 1 large can plus 1 small can whole tomatoes, crushed by hand with juices
ingredients.raw: 1 large can plus 1 small can whole [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], crushed by hand with juices

ingredients.display: ½ cup (120 ml), plus more as needed, white table wine
ingredients.raw: ½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]), plus more as needed, white table [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]

lead: This is a more rustic and less "Italian-American" recipe than the other one.

procedure.text: Heat the olive oil and almond oil in an oversized pan. Add onion, garlic, and bell pepper, and sweat.
Deglaze pan with white wine, then add tomatoes.
Grind dried herbs and red pepper flakes with a mortar and pestle. Add this mixture and the unreserved fresh basil to the pan.
Simmer for an hour (or more if necessary), stirring occasionally.
Add wine until desired consistency is achieved. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add al dente pasta to pan with sauce and combine using tongs.
Plate and garnish with fresh basil and Parmigiano-Reggiano.

sections.heading: Notes, tips, and variations
sections.text: * To save time, make the sauce the night before you plan to serve it. Chill overnight, and reheat it over low heat while you cook the pasta. The overnight rest period also allows for flavor development and sweetness.

title: American Marinara Sauce II
